options.a: Deadlines are targets, and a party may perform within a reasonable time after
options.b: The closing date is binding, but contingency deadlines may be extended freely
options.c: The contract must close within 30 days of acceptance to remain enforceable
options.d: Contract dates and times are critical and late performance may be a breach

distractorExplanations.a: That is the reasonable-time standard that applies when the clause is absent; the clause makes dates strict.
distractorExplanations.b: The clause applies to all contract dates, including contingency deadlines, not just the closing date.
distractorExplanations.c: The clause enforces the dates the parties chose; it does not impose a fixed 30-day closing period.

options.a: Proceed as a dual agent after giving the buyer written notice of the relationship
options.b: Switch to representing the buyer while keeping the seller's listing active for both
options.c: Terminate the listing agreement unilaterally and refund the seller's marketing costs
options.d: Not create the dual agency relationship; consider designated agency, referral, or withdrawal

distractorExplanations.a: Dual agency requires informed consent from both parties; notice to the buyer alone cannot replace the seller's consent.
distractorExplanations.b: Representing the buyer while still holding the listing is undisclosed dual agency, the exact thing the seller refused.
distractorExplanations.c: Refusing dual agency does not let the broker abandon the listing; the broker simply declines to represent the buyer.

options.a: Obtain the highest price by carrying out every seller instruction, lawful or not
options.b: Owe the buyer customer the same loyalty and confidentiality as the seller
options.c: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law
options.d: Guarantee the seller a closed sale at list price within the listing term

distractorExplanations.a: Obedience extends only to lawful instructions; a broker must refuse illegal directions such as discriminatory or fraudulent ones.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses client and customer: a buyer customer is owed honesty and fair dealing, not the fiduciary loyalty owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.d: Fiduciary duties concern conduct (loyalty, care, obedience), not guaranteed outcomes; brokers cannot promise a sale or price.

options.a: The seller's reason for selling and lowest acceptable price, even if the seller objects
options.b: Known latent defects or conditions that could significantly affect value or desirability
options.c: The racial or religious makeup of the neighborhood, since it may affect desirability
options.d: Obvious patent defects, while hidden latent defects are left for the buyer's own inspection

distractorExplanations.a: Seller motivation and bottom-line price are confidential client information, not material property facts a buyer must be told.
distractorExplanations.c: Commenting on a neighborhood's race or religion is steering under the Fair Housing Act, not a required material-fact disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: Reverses the rule: known latent (hidden) defects are exactly what must be disclosed, because a buyer cannot readily discover them.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Material property defects and legally required disclosures must be shared, as required by law; confidential motivations may be protected.

options.a: Public use and the owner's consent
options.b: Payment of the property's assessed value
options.c: A police-power finding without compensation
options.d: Public use/purpose and just compensation

distractorExplanations.a: Eminent domain is a forced taking; the owner's consent is not required, which is what distinguishes condemnation from a voluntary sale.
distractorExplanations.b: Just compensation is based on fair market value, not the tax assessor's assessed value, which is often lower.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses eminent domain with police power: zoning and code regulation need no compensation, but a taking does.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Takings require public use/purpose and just compensation under the Fifth Amendment (constitutional framework).

options.a: Upon the death of the remainderman
options.b: Upon the death of the measuring life
options.c: When the life tenant sells the estate
options.d: Upon the death of the original grantor

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses the remainderman with the measuring life; if the remainderman dies first, the remainder passes to his heirs and the life estate continues.
distractorExplanations.c: A life tenant may convey the interest, but the buyer simply holds a life estate pur autre vie that still ends at the original tenant's death.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the grantor with the measuring life; the grantor's death does not end an estate measured by the life tenant's life.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Life estates are measured by a life; the estate ends when the measuring life dies (or as otherwise defined in the grant), and the remainder or reversion follows.

options.a: A zoning variance granted to the owner for a hardship use
options.b: A deed recorded with a full covenant of warranty from the grantor
options.c: The abstract summary of the chain of title prepared for a buyer
options.d: A claim, encumbrance, or defect that may impair marketability

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses public land-use control with title: a variance governs permitted use and is not a claim against ownership.
distractorExplanations.b: A recorded general warranty deed strengthens the chain of title; it is the opposite of a cloud that casts doubt on it.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses an abstract of title (a history of recorded documents) with a cloud, which is a defect or claim the abstract may reveal.

options.a: Delivering the signed deed to the grantee
options.b: Recording the deed in the public land records
options.c: Having the deed acknowledged before a notary
options.d: Sending written notice to each adjoining owner

distractorExplanations.a: Delivery and acceptance transfer title between the parties, but they do not give the world constructive notice.
distractorExplanations.c: Acknowledgment is what makes a deed eligible for recording; the notice to the world comes from recording itself.
distractorExplanations.d: Notifying specific people gives them actual notice only; constructive notice to everyone comes from the public record.

options.a: Interest alone, with the full principal due as a balloon at maturity
options.b: Both interest and principal so the balance declines over the term
options.c: Part of the interest, with the unpaid rest added to the balance
options.d: Interest plus escrowed taxes and insurance, with no principal reduction

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an interest-only or balloon loan; an amortizing payment repays principal with each installment.
distractorExplanations.c: Adding unpaid interest to the balance is negative amortization, the opposite of a fully amortizing payment.
distractorExplanations.d: Escrowed taxes and insurance may be added to PITI, but an amortizing payment still reduces principal every month.

options.a: A VA loan is made with zero down payment
options.b: Conventional LTV is low (commonly below 80%)
options.c: The seller pays two discount points at closing
options.d: Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)

distractorExplanations.a: VA loans charge a funding fee instead of PMI; PMI applies to conventional loans with thin equity.
distractorExplanations.b: Reverses the threshold: PMI is required when LTV is above 80%, and it can be dropped once equity reaches 20%.
distractorExplanations.c: Discount points buy down the interest rate; who pays them has nothing to do with whether PMI is required.

options.a: Can adjust based on an index plus margin, subject to caps
options.b: Can adjust whenever the lender chooses, without caps
options.c: Adjusts with the margin while the index stays fixed
options.d: Changes only when the borrower refinances the loan

distractorExplanations.b: ARM changes follow a published index on set adjustment dates, and periodic and lifetime caps limit each change.
distractorExplanations.c: Reverses the terms: the margin is fixed for the loan's life, and the index is the variable part that moves.
distractorExplanations.d: A refinance replaces the loan with a new note; an ARM's rate resets on scheduled adjustment dates under the existing note.

options.a: The listing broker earns a commission unless the seller personally finds the buyer, in which case no fee is owed
options.b: The seller may list with several brokers at once and pays the one broker who first procures a ready buyer
options.c: The buyer's agent, rather than the listing broker, is owed the commission whenever that agent introduced the buyer
options.d: The listing broker is owed a commission if the property sells during the term, regardless of who finds the buyer

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an exclusive agency listing, where a sale the owner procures personally owes no commission.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes an open listing, where only the procuring broker is paid and several brokers may list at once.
distractorExplanations.c: Swaps the party: the exclusive right-to-sell agreement protects the listing broker's commission, not the buyer's agent's.

options.a: Avoid acting as the buyer's advocate and stay within the listing agency role
options.b: Prepare a CMA for the buyer and recommend an offer amount, then tell the seller about it later
options.c: Give pricing advice to the buyer, since a customer is owed the same duties as a client
options.d: Tell the buyer the seller's lowest acceptable price so the parties agree faster

distractorExplanations.b: Recommending an offer price is buyer advocacy; doing it for a customer creates undisclosed dual agency, which later notice does not cure.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses customer duties (honesty, disclosure of material facts) with the fiduciary advocacy owed only to a client.
distractorExplanations.d: Disclosing the seller's bottom line breaches the listing agent's duty of confidentiality to the seller client.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Listing agents represent the seller; advocacy for a buyer requires a proper agency shift/disclosure. If the buyer wants advocacy, the licensee may properly create buyer agency (with any required dual-agency disclosure and consent) where allowed.

options.a: Signed after the offer had been revoked
options.b: Later found a lower-priced comparable home
options.c: Agreed to a contract with an illegal purpose
options.d: Was induced by fraud or was a minor

distractorExplanations.a: Acceptance after revocation means no contract was formed at all; that is not a voidable contract.
distractorExplanations.b: Buyer's remorse over a better deal is not a legal ground to avoid a valid contract; fraud or incapacity is.
distractorExplanations.c: A contract for an illegal purpose is void (unenforceable by anyone), not voidable at one party's option.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Fraud or lack of capacity can make a contract voidable by the protected party. Whether the protected party may avoid the contract depends on the circumstances (e.g., ratification after reaching majority).

options.a: The seller may sell the property personally without owing any commission
options.b: The broker is paid a flat fee whether or not the property sells
options.c: The broker keeps the buyer's earnest money as the commission at closing
options.d: The broker's compensation is the amount above a seller's net price

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an exclusive agency listing; it is not why net listings are restricted.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes a flat-fee arrangement; a net listing pays the broker whatever exceeds the seller's net figure.
distractorExplanations.c: Earnest money is trust money credited per the contract; a net listing is defined by pay above the seller's net price.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Net listings can incentivize underpricing relative to the seller's interests and are banned or tightly regulated in many places. That structure creates conflict-of-interest concerns because the broker gains by underpricing the seller's net figure.

options.a: A right to purchase on stated terms within a period, usually for consideration
options.b: An obligation to purchase on stated terms within a period, usually with earnest money
options.c: A right of first refusal to match any offer the owner accepts
options.d: A leasehold that converts into ownership once the scheduled rent payments are made

distractorExplanations.b: That describes a bilateral purchase contract; an option gives the optionee a right, not an obligation, to buy.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses an option with a right of first refusal, which only lets the holder match a third-party offer the owner accepts.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes a rent-to-own or contract-for-deed arrangement; an option is a purchased right to buy on fixed terms.

options.a: A misstatement of a measurable fact, such as square footage, made to induce a sale
options.b: A negligent misrepresentation the licensee should have known was untrue
options.c: Exaggerated opinion that a reasonable person would not treat as a factual warranty
options.d: An implied warranty of habitability the seller gives through the ad wording

distractorExplanations.a: A false statement of measurable fact is misrepresentation, not puffing; puffing is non-factual opinion.
distractorExplanations.b: Negligent misrepresentation involves a false fact the licensee should have verified; puffing is opinion, not fact.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses puffing with a warranty; puffing is exaggerated opinion that a reasonable buyer would not rely on as a warranty.

options.a: Practicing law whenever they fill in names, prices, and dates on the form
options.b: Practicing law if they draft novel legal clauses beyond authorized forms
options.c: Required to have each completed form approved by a closing attorney first
options.d: Acting as an escrow agent once the buyer's earnest money is listed on the form

distractorExplanations.a: Filling in the factual blanks of an approved form is ordinary licensee work; drafting novel legal clauses is the problem.
distractorExplanations.c: No attorney pre-approval is required to complete approved forms; the line is drafting new legal language.
distractorExplanations.d: Recording the earnest money amount on a form does not make the licensee an escrow agent; this confuses roles.

options.a: Depositing several clients' earnest money into one pooled trust account
options.b: Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds improperly
options.c: Converting client trust money to the broker's own use and spending it
options.d: Holding earnest money in trust until closing instead of paying the seller

distractorExplanations.a: A pooled trust account holding only client money is normal and allowed; commingling mixes trust money with broker funds.
distractorExplanations.c: That is conversion (misappropriation), a separate and more serious violation than commingling.
distractorExplanations.d: Holding deposits in trust until closing is the proper procedure, not commingling with personal or operating funds.

options.a: Survivorship
options.b: Reversion
options.c: Remainder
options.d: Dower rights

distractorExplanations.b: Reversion is the grantor's future interest after a lesser estate such as a life estate ends, not a joint tenancy feature.
distractorExplanations.c: A remainder is a future interest that follows a life estate; joint tenancy is defined by survivorship among co-owners.
distractorExplanations.d: Dower is a surviving wife's marital interest (abolished in most states), not a feature of joint tenancy.

options.a: May hold unequal shares and typically lack survivorship unless specified
options.b: Must hold equal shares but may each leave their interest to heirs by will
options.c: Share the four unities of time, title, interest, and possession
options.d: Cannot sell their share without written consent of the other co-owners

distractorExplanations.b: Equal shares are a joint-tenancy unity; tenants in common may hold unequal shares.
distractorExplanations.c: The four unities describe joint tenancy; tenants in common share only the unity of possession.
distractorExplanations.d: A tenant in common may freely sell or encumber their undivided share without the other co-owners' consent.

options.a: Prior use allowed to continue after a new zoning law is adopted
options.b: Permanent change of the zoning map for an entire district
options.c: Permission to deviate from a zoning requirement due to hardship
options.d: Use the zoning code allows in a district subject to stated conditions

distractorExplanations.a: That is a legal nonconforming (grandfathered) use, not a variance granted for hardship.
distractorExplanations.d: That is a conditional use or special-use permit, which the code anticipates; a variance relieves a hardship.
distractorExplanations.b: That is rezoning/amendment.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Variances grant relief from strict zoning application in hardship cases. The variance is granted by the zoning authority (e.g., a board of adjustment).

options.a: Land bordering flowing water such as a river or stream
options.b: Land bordering a lake, sea, or ocean with a tidal shoreline
options.c: Groundwater beneath a parcel drawn through a private well
options.d: Water permits issued by the state under prior appropriation

distractorExplanations.b: Rights along lakes, seas, and oceans are littoral rights; riparian rights concern flowing water.
distractorExplanations.c: Groundwater is percolating water governed by separate rules; riparian rights attach to land along flowing water.
distractorExplanations.d: Prior appropriation is a competing permit-based doctrine, not the riparian doctrine tied to bordering land.

options.a: 1% of the loan amount
options.b: 1% of the purchase price
options.c: 1% of the down payment
options.d: 1% of the interest rate

distractorExplanations.b: Confuses the loan amount with the price; a point is based on the loan, which is usually smaller than the price.
distractorExplanations.c: Points are computed on the loan amount, not on the buyer's down payment.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the cost of a point with its effect; a point costs 1% of the loan, not 1% of the rate.

options.a: Prohibiting discrimination in mortgage lending based on race or sex
options.b: Banning certain kickbacks and requiring settlement cost disclosures
options.c: Requiring APR disclosure and a right to rescind certain refinances
options.d: Setting the maximum interest rate lenders may charge on home loans

distractorExplanations.a: That is the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Fair Housing Act, not RESPA's settlement-cost focus.
distractorExplanations.c: APR disclosure and rescission rights come from the Truth in Lending Act, not RESPA.
distractorExplanations.d: Interest-rate ceilings come from state usury laws; RESPA does not cap rates.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: RESPA addresses settlement services, kickbacks, and related disclosures (with TRID integration for many loans). These protections apply in covered federally related transactions.

options.a: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays off early, when the note allows it
options.b: Requires an extra charge when the borrower pays after the grace period
options.c: Allows the lender to demand full payment if the property is sold or transferred
options.d: Allows the lender to declare the whole balance due after a missed payment

distractorExplanations.b: That is a late-payment charge, not a fee for paying the loan off early.
distractorExplanations.c: That is a due-on-sale (alienation) clause, not a prepayment penalty.
distractorExplanations.d: That is an acceleration clause triggered by default, not a charge for early payoff.

options.a: Borrower default on the mortgage note
options.b: Covered title defects and claims against ownership
options.c: Fire, wind, and flood damage to the structure
options.d: Undisclosed defects in the home's systems found after closing

distractorExplanations.a: Default risk is covered by mortgage insurance (PMI/FHA MIP), not title insurance.
distractorExplanations.c: Casualty damage is covered by hazard and flood insurance, not title insurance.
distractorExplanations.d: Physical system failures are the subject of a home warranty or disclosure claim, not title insurance.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Owner's/lender's title policies insure against covered title risks, not casualty. Coverage is defined by the owner's or lender's policy terms and exceptions.

options.a: The seller is charged; it reduces the seller's net proceeds
options.b: The buyer receives a credit reducing cash to close
options.c: The item is prorated and split evenly between buyer and seller
options.d: The buyer is charged; it increases cash needed

distractorExplanations.a: Swaps the party: a buyer debit charges the buyer, not the seller.
distractorExplanations.c: Proration splits an expense by time, and each share then appears as a debit or credit; it is not what 'debit' means.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes a credit.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Debits charge a party; buyer debits typically increase funds due at closing. A debit to the seller, by contrast, reduces the seller's proceeds.

options.a: Originate new purchase loans directly to borrowers at the closing table
options.b: Buy and sell existing mortgages, improving liquidity for originators
options.c: Insure lenders against borrower default on low-down-payment loans
options.d: Set the federal funds rate that lenders use to price mortgages

distractorExplanations.a: Originating loans to borrowers is the primary mortgage market, not the secondary market.
distractorExplanations.c: Default insurance is the role of PMI or FHA mortgage insurance, not the secondary market.
distractorExplanations.d: The Federal Reserve sets the federal funds target; the secondary market buys and sells loans.

options.a: Maximum loan-to-value ratios lenders may approve on home loans
options.b: Required disclosure of the APR and total finance charges
options.c: Maximum interest rates that may be charged on certain loans
options.d: Minimum down payments required for conventional mortgages

distractorExplanations.a: Loan-to-value limits are underwriting or investor rules, not usury law.
distractorExplanations.b: APR and finance-charge disclosure come from the Truth in Lending Act, not usury law.
distractorExplanations.d: Down payment minimums are set by lenders and investors, not by usury statutes.

options.a: Finance construction draws that convert into a permanent mortgage once the home is complete
options.b: Fund a 30-year fully amortizing primary residence as the only permanent loan
options.c: Combine a first mortgage with a second loan to avoid paying PMI on the purchase
options.d: Finance a short-term gap, often between purchase of a new home and sale of an existing one

distractorExplanations.a: That is a construction-to-permanent loan, not a short-term bridge between two home transactions.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a piggyback (80/10/10) structure, not short-term gap financing.
distractorExplanations.b: That is a permanent mortgage.

options.a: Generally improper/misleading and can be a license law violation
options.b: Allowed if the licensee puts the profit promise in writing
options.c: Acceptable puffing as long as the buyer is an investor
options.d: Permitted if the broker of record approves the promise in advance in writing

distractorExplanations.b: Putting a profit promise in writing does not make it truthful; it is still a misleading assurance.
distractorExplanations.c: A specific promise of future profit is a factual assurance, not puffing, and buyer type does not change that.
distractorExplanations.d: Broker approval cannot authorize a misleading promise; the supervising broker would share the violation.

options.a: May keep closing pending deals for up to 90 days but may not take new listings
options.b: May practice under the broker's license while the renewal application is pending
options.c: May not engage in activities requiring an active license until renewed/reactivated
options.d: May still earn referral fees on new deals as long as CE is completed later

distractorExplanations.a: There is no grace period to keep brokering pending deals; all licensed activity stops while the license is not active.
distractorExplanations.b: A licensee cannot operate under the broker's license; their own license must be active.
distractorExplanations.d: Referral fees for new deals are licensed compensation and require an active license at the time of the activity.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-ga-licens.explanation: Active status is required for licensed activity. The license must be properly renewed or reactivated first.

options.a: Legal if disclosed on the Closing Disclosure
options.b: Permitted when paid by a title company
options.c: Restricted under federal RESPA rules
options.d: Regulated by TILA, not by RESPA

distractorExplanations.a: Disclosure does not cure a prohibited Section 8 referral fee; RESPA bans the kickback itself.
distractorExplanations.b: Title companies are settlement service providers, so their referral payments are squarely covered by RESPA Section 8.
distractorExplanations.d: TILA governs credit-cost disclosures; referral kickbacks are a RESPA Section 8 issue.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-ga-licens.explanation: RESPA bans certain referral fees; state ethics/license rules also police improper inducements. Improper inducements can also violate state license-law standards of practice.

options.a: Promptly as required by agency and license rules
options.b: Within five business days after the offer is received
options.c: After any earlier offer has been accepted or rejected first
options.d: Once the buyer's lender has issued a written pre-approval

distractorExplanations.b: Invents a five-day window; offers must be presented promptly, not on a fixed delay.
distractorExplanations.c: Offers are not held for sequential handling; each must be presented promptly, even while another is pending.
distractorExplanations.d: Lender pre-approval is not a precondition to presenting an offer; the seller decides how to weigh financing.

options.a: Allowed once the listing agreement has expired
options.b: A serious breach of fiduciary/license duties
options.c: Permitted if the licensee pays full list price
options.d: A RESPA matter handled by the CFPB, not the state

distractorExplanations.a: The duty of confidentiality survives the end of the agency, so expiration does not permit self-dealing.
distractorExplanations.c: Paying list price does not cure undisclosed self-dealing with confidential client information.
distractorExplanations.d: Wrong body: this is a fiduciary and license-law breach for the state regulator, not a RESPA settlement-cost issue.

options.a: Moves with the departing associate, who becomes the records custodian
options.b: Remains with the brokerage; the firm retains responsibility for records
options.c: Is transferred to the state commission for storage until retention ends
options.d: Stays with the brokerage for pending deals, while closed files go to the associate

distractorExplanations.a: Transaction files belong to the brokerage, which stays the custodian after an associate leaves.
distractorExplanations.c: The regulator does not store brokerage files; the firm keeps them for the required retention period.
distractorExplanations.d: Closed files also stay with the brokerage, which must produce them for audits during the retention period.

options.a: Discipline only if the crime was a felony
options.b: Review by the local REALTOR® board ethics panel
options.c: License suspension/revocation proceedings
options.d: A fine but no action against the license

distractorExplanations.a: Crimes of moral turpitude can trigger discipline even as misdemeanors; felony status is not the test.
distractorExplanations.b: Wrong body: an association can discipline members but cannot suspend or revoke a state license.
distractorExplanations.d: Convictions related to practice can lead to suspension or revocation, not merely a fine.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-ga-licens.explanation: Criminal convictions can trigger disciplinary cases. Those proceedings are brought before the Georgia Real Estate Commission.

options.a: They let the broker withdraw earned interest as personal income
options.b: They replace the need to keep separate ledgers for each client
options.c: They are filed with the IRS each month to report escrow interest
options.d: They help detect shortages/overages and demonstrate compliance

distractorExplanations.a: Reconciliation is a control, not a payout mechanism; trust interest follows statutory rules, not broker income.
distractorExplanations.b: Reconciliation compares the bank balance to the client ledgers, so it depends on those ledgers rather than replacing them.
distractorExplanations.c: Reconciliations are kept for regulator audits, not filed monthly with the IRS.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-ga-licens.explanation: Regular reconciliation is a core trust-account control. Regulators such as the Georgia Real Estate Commission review these records in trust-account audits.

options.a: Prohibited or restricted by advertising rules
options.b: Allowed if the agent's phone number is included
options.c: Permitted when an agent sells their own property
options.d: Allowed on social media but not in print ads

distractorExplanations.b: A phone number does not identify the licensee or the brokerage, so the ad is still blind.
distractorExplanations.c: Licensees advertising their own property must still disclose licensee status; that is a common blind-ad trap.
distractorExplanations.d: Advertising identification rules apply to online and social media ads just as to print.
